requirements.statement: The notification hub's browser title is 'Overview - Import notification service - GOV.UK' and its main heading is 'Overview'.
requirements.why: The hub is the top of the notification in Design Release 2.1, named Overview.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p5-003 and trace-animals-fit-p4-002 show the title and the extra-large 'Overview' heading today, and repo-tests-p3-066 proves the H1 end to end.

requirements.statement: Each live-animals notification has its own hub page in the live-animals set, addressed by the notification at the set's own notification path (/live-animals/notifications/{reference}).
requirements.why: The real service stores many notifications per trader, so the hub must say which one it shows; the prototype holds a single notification in its session and cannot express this, and the prototype never decides URL paths.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p5-001 serves the hub per notification under the live-animals set, and repo-tests-p3-066 proves it end to end; c-128 keeps it over the prototype's single /notification-hub route for whichever notification is in the session.

requirements.statement: Above the 'Overview' heading the hub shows the notification's status as a tag ('Draft' until it is submitted) and the notification reference, which the notification already has before any task is answered, in the form 'GBN-AG-', a two-digit year, a hyphen and six upper-case letters or digits (for example GBN-AG-26-DGWJ47).
requirements.why: The trader always sees which notification they are on and what state it is in.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p5-061 and trace-animals-fit-p4-003 show the shared journey strip with a 'Draft' tag and the reference above the heading today, and trace-animals-fit-p4-004 shows every reference already in the GBN-AG-26-XXXXXX form from the first page; trace-animals-fit-p4-066 records that no trace shows the hub for a notification that is no longer a draft. The notification type label the design now puts before the reference is its own requirement.

requirements.statement: In the status strip above the page heading, the notification reference is preceded by the notification's type label and ' - ': 'Live animals - GBN-AG-26-7K8M2P' in the live-animals set and 'Germinal products - <reference>' in the germinal-products set. In the high-risk plants frontend the strip reads the label plants' own commodity type question gives the chosen type, then ' - ' and the reference, and the reference alone until a commodity type is chosen. The strip is shared, so the hub and every other page that shows it read the same.
requirements.why: The design names the notification's type beside its reference so the trader sees what kind of notification they are on; the 9 October afternoon ruling has plants take the same change in the same increment while keeping its own answers and wording, and plants' types are worded differently from the prototype's demo labels (c-notification-hub-001).
requirements.deltaNote: Today the strip shows the status tag and the reference alone, with no type label: repo-frontend-p5-061 and trace-animals-fit-p4-003 in live animals, repo-plantsfrontend-p2-008 in plants.

requirements.statement: Opening the hub leaves the notification saved as a draft: nothing a trader has answered is lost by leaving from the hub.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 saves the draft when the hub opens; the real service already saves each page's answers to the notification record as it goes.
requirements.deltaNote: trace-e2e-p13-044-m1 shows every saved page committing to the stored notification (the concurrency token rises per save), so the draft is already saved whenever the hub shows.

requirements.statement: While a submitted notification is being amended (status 'Amend'), the hub's status line also shows a 'Cancel amend' link-style control, which goes to the cancel-amendment confirmation page the review page uses. The control comes from the shared status strip, so the live-animals, germinal-products and high-risk plants Overview pages all show it.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's shared status line offers Cancel amend on every page that includes it, and the hub's missing modal include is a prototype omission; the 9 October afternoon ruling keeps the Amend bar's 'Cancel amend' going to a confirmation page rather than a pop-up, changes it in the shared strip because every set that amends needs it, and holds the pop-up back as a waiting-on-design question. Building it in the shared strip means the plants Overview needs no work of its own. The 27 November ruling builds the germinal set's cancel amendment on what the manage notifications theme lands.
requirements.deltaNote: The real hub's strip shows only the tag and reference (repo-frontend-p5-061), and the plants hub offers no cancel-amendment link at all (repo-plantsfrontend-p2-008); cancel amend is offered today only from the review page and the dashboard. Built by the shared strip change, which reaches every set's hub at once.

requirements.statement: The hub has no back link; the ways off it are the 'Return to dashboard' button and the service navigation.
requirements.why: The hub is the top of the notification, not a step in it.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p5-060 and trace-animals-fit-p4-005 show no back link on the hub today.

requirements.statement: The hub shows a 'Your commodities' heading (h2) above the commodity total cards, on every visit, including before any commodity is chosen.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 opens the hub with the consignment totals.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p5-005 and trace-animals-fit-p4-007 show the 'Your commodities' h2 from the first visit today.

requirements.statement: For a live-animals notification the first card shows the total number of animals, labelled 'Animals' with the caption 'Total number of animals in this consignment'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 copy for the animals total card.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p5-007 and trace-animals-fit-p4-008 show the 'Animals' label and caption verbatim today, and trace-animals-fit-p4-013 shows the entered count appearing in the card.

requirements.statement: The hub shows a card for the total number of packages, labelled 'Packages/boxes' with the caption 'Total number of packages in this consignment', in the live-animals set and in the germinal-products set alike.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 copy for the packages total card, which the germinal hub carries with the same caption.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p5-008 and trace-animals-fit-p4-009 show the 'Packages/boxes' label and caption verbatim on the live-animals hub today; the germinal hub takes it with its copy of the hub (req-1836).

requirements.statement: A commodity total card reads '0' when its total is not above zero. The animals and packages totals add up the counts saved against the notification's commodity lines, a blank or non-numeric count adding nothing, in the live-animals and the germinal-products sets.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 counts only positive entries, so a card never shows a negative or odd total.
requirements.deltaNote: Already met on the live-animals hub: the totals sum the lines' counts (repo-frontend-p5-009), a blank or non-numeric count is treated as nothing (repo-frontend-p5-010), and both cards read 0 before any line exists and while a chosen commodity still owes its numbers (repo-frontend-p5-011, trace-animals-fit-p4-011, trace-animals-fit-p4-012, trace-e2e-p13-015). The germinal hub takes the same rule with its copy. The validation that keeps a zero, negative or fractional count out of the record belongs to the commodity-details area.

requirements.statement: In the germinal-products set, the hub's 'Your commodities' shows a quantity card labelled 'Units/pieces' with the caption 'Total quantity in this consignment', then the 'Packages/boxes' card, and no 'Animals' card and no weight card.
requirements.why: The design counts germinal products by quantity and packages, not by animals, and its hub shows no weight card; the data specification gives germinal products a quantity in units or pieces on each commodity line, and each set holds one category, so the germinal hub never mixes in an animals count.
requirements.deltaNote: No germinal-products set exists today, and the only hub always shows the Animals and Packages/boxes cards (trace-animals-fit-p4-008). Built in the germinal set's copy of the hub.

requirements.statement: In the germinal-products set, the 'Units/pieces' card shows the total of the quantity (units or pieces) answers saved against the notification's commodity lines that are positive numbers, and '0' when the total is not above zero.
requirements.why: The design's rule for the germinal quantity card; the quantity it totals is the data specification's commodity-line quantity in units or pieces, not the prototype's storage.
requirements.deltaNote: No germinal-products set or quantity card exists today. The prototype sums its own numberOfPackages answers for this card (prototype-dr2-1-source-p12-116 note); the real card totals whatever field the germinal set stores the quantity in.

requirements.statement: In the germinal-products set, the hub shows a 'Kilograms' card totalling the gross weight in kilograms entered for the consignment.
requirements.why: Out of scope: the design no longer shows a weight card on the germinal hub, and nothing ranked above it asks for one; the 9 October ruling fixes what the germinal set stores as weight, not that the hub shows it (c-244).
requirements.deltaNote: No germinal-products set or weight card exists today.

requirements.statement: Each commodity total card is a static panel (no link or button) that reads the number, then the label, then the caption, with the number and the label larger than the caption and the caption wrapping to no more than two lines; the cards sit side by side on a wide screen and stack with no horizontal scrolling on a 360px screen.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 shows the totals as value, label and caption tiles; the real hub already draws them that way from GOV.UK design tokens, because no GOV.UK Frontend component renders such a panel.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p5-006 and repo-frontend-p5-012 to p5-014, with trace-animals-fit-p4-014 to p4-018, show static number-label-caption panels, side by side and stacking on a small screen, built as a custom block from GOV.UK tokens, today.

requirements.statement: On the live-animals hub, assistive technology can move by region: the two total cards are regions labelled 'Animals summary' and 'Packages summary', and the 'Your commodities' block, the task list and each numbered section are regions named by their own heading.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 marks these regions up for screen-reader users, and the 9 October afternoon ruling's regions change reaches plants in the same increment.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the two cards are regions named 'Animals summary' and 'Packages summary' (repo-frontend-p5-007, repo-frontend-p5-008) and each numbered section is a region holding one task list (repo-frontend-p5-017). What is left is the task list as a whole being a region named by its 'Notification task list' heading (repo-frontend-p5-015 shows only the heading), as the plants hub's already is (repo-plantsfrontend-p2-011).

requirements.statement: On a notification's hub the task list sits below the commodity totals under a second-level heading reading 'Notification task list'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 gives the task list its own heading, and the owner's 19 November decision fixes the wording as 'Notification task list', 'task list' being the GOV.UK spelling, in the live animals and the plants services alike.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p5-015 renders the 'Notification task list' h2 between the commodity totals and the first group today, in the owner's spelling; DR1 had already landed the heading itself (document-dr1-parity-backlog-p4-046) in the one-word spelling the older traces show, which the code has since changed.

requirements.statement: For a notification, the task list has exactly five numbered sections with h3 headings, in this order: '1. About the consignment', '2. Description of the goods', '3. Transport and arrival', '4. Documents', '5. Addresses', and nothing after them (no contact address section and no review task row), and a journey section that owns no task row is left off the hub.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 gives the hub five numbered sections, ending with Addresses, and ends it with buttons rather than a review row; the owner's 17 November decision fixes the fifth section's words as 'Addresses' and keeps its number.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p5-082 shows the five section headings verbatim and in order, the fifth reading '5. Addresses', with no contact address section and nothing after them, and repo-frontend-p5-018 leaves out a journey section that carries no row. The older traces still show six sections, '5. Consignment parties' and '6. Contact address' (trace-animals-fit-p4-021, trace-e2e-p13-018), which the code has since changed (c-406).

requirements.statement: The third row of section 1 reads 'Main import reason', in English and in the Welsh copy.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 names the task 'Main import reason'; DR1 named it after its own prototype, which is not a judgement departing from the design, so Design Release 2.1 wins.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p5-024 shows the row titled 'Main import reason' today, with a Welsh entry for the same key (repo-frontend-p5-079); the older traces still show 'Main reason for import' (trace-animals-fit-p4-028, trace-e2e-p13-020), which the code has since changed.

requirements.statement: Section 1 holds, in order, 'Where is this consignment coming from?', 'What are you importing?' and the main import reason row; it has no exit details row, and the import reason row is complete only once the reason and any follow-up it reveals are answered (Re-entry alone completes it).
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 shows three rows in section 1, keeping the row label 'Where is this consignment coming from?' although its page is headed 'Origin of the import'; DR1 already folded exit details into the import reason task.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p5-019, p5-022 and p5-023 show the three rows in this order today, with no exit details row among the eleven the hub holds (repo-frontend-p5-083), and DR1 removed that row (document-dr1-parity-backlog-p4-026); the 'exit details' row the e2e spec still names (trace-e2e-p13-026) is never shown.

requirements.statement: 'Commodity details' is its own row, first in section 2, shown from a fresh notification as 'To do'; it reads 'Complete' once the number of animals (and packages where asked) is saved for every chosen commodity, while 'What are you importing?' reads 'Complete' as soon as a commodity is chosen. Opening it before a commodity is chosen shows the 'What are you importing?' question instead.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 splits choosing the commodity from giving its numbers.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p5-020, p5-025, p5-045, p5-049 and p5-050, with trace-animals-fit-p4-032 to p4-035, show the separate row, first in section 2, live with 'To do' from the start and redirecting to the commodity question when nothing is chosen, as Design Release 2.1 does (trace-prototype-dr2-1-p12-016); this settles the open DR1 gating call (document-dr1-parity-backlog-p4-043) as the status quo.

requirements.statement: 'Identification details' shows in section 2, after 'Commodity details', only when a chosen commodity needs animal identifiers, and is absent otherwise (for example before a commodity is chosen, or for poultry).
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 asks for identifiers only for the commodities that need them.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p5-040 to p5-042 and trace-e2e-p13-022 and p13-023 show the row absent until a commodity carrying identifiers is chosen, then placed after Commodity details. Which commodities carry identifiers, and what makes the row complete, belong to the animal-identification area; trace-animals-fit-p4-063 and p4-064 record that no trace exercises a multi-species or identifier-free commodity.

requirements.statement: In the live-animals set, section 2 always shows 'Additional details', after 'Commodity details' and after 'Identification details' where that applies.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 shows the additional animal details task wherever that page is required, and every live-animals notification owes it, with each set holding one category. The germinal half is a requirement of its own.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p5-040 makes only Identification details and Transit countries conditional, so 'Additional details' is always shown today (trace-e2e-p13-021, trace-animals-fit-p4-042), which is what the live-animals set needs once its catalogue holds only live animals.

requirements.statement: In the germinal-products set, section 2 holds 'Commodity details', then 'Identification details' where a chosen commodity needs identifiers, and no other row: there is no 'Additional details' row and no 'Total gross weight' row, the total gross weight being asked for each species on the commodity details page and counted by the 'Commodity details' row.
requirements.why: The design leaves the additional details task off the germinal hub, and the germinal set has no additional details page; the owner's 27 November decision keeps the germinal total gross weight per species, so the design's separate once-per-notification gross weight task has no page to open (c-notification-hub-002).
requirements.deltaNote: No germinal-products set exists today; the live hub's section 2 holds Commodity details, Identification details and Additional details (repo-frontend-p5-020).

requirements.statement: In the germinal-products set, section 2 shows a 'Total gross weight' row after 'Commodity details', opening a page that asks the consignment's total gross weight once for the whole notification, complete once that weight is given.
requirements.why: Out of scope: the owner's 27 November decision keeps the germinal total gross weight per species, asked on the commodity details page, so the design's separate gross weight page and its hub row are not built (c-notification-hub-002).
requirements.deltaNote: No germinal-products set exists today.

requirements.statement: Section 3 always shows 'Arrival details', which opens even before a commodity is chosen, and 'Transport details'; each reads 'Complete' once its answers are saved.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 rows for arrival and transport, keeping the row label 'Transport details' although its page is headed 'Transporter details'.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p5-028 and p5-030 hold both rows in section 3 today, and repo-frontend-p5-084, p5-046 and trace-animals-fit-p4-044 and p4-045 show Arrival details opening and completing before a commodity is chosen.

requirements.statement: In the live-animals set, 'Transit countries' shows in section 3, between 'Arrival details' and 'Transport details', only when transit countries are required for the notification (for example for a journey by road or rail, and not by air or sea), and reads 'Complete' once at least one transit country is selected; saved with none it reads 'To do'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 decides from the notification whether transit countries are owed, and shows the row only then. The germinal half is a requirement of its own.
requirements.deltaNote: The row is hidden only while its page's gate is shut (repo-frontend-p5-039, repo-frontend-p5-040), so it appears once arrival details are saved even with no commodity chosen and the transit page skipped (trace-animals-fit-p4-047, p4-048); Design Release 2.1 shows it only when transit countries are required. The rule that decides when they are required belongs to the arrival-and-transit area.

requirements.statement: For a notification, section '4. Documents' holds the single row 'Upload documents', which reads 'Complete' once at least one document is uploaded and otherwise 'To do', and never stops the notification reaching review or submission.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 treats documents as optional.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p5-034 and trace-animals-fit-p4-050 and p4-051 show the single 'Upload documents' row, 'To do' while the rest is complete, with the review still open; trace-e2e-p13-033 shows the notification submittable without documents, and trace-animals-fit-p4-065 records that no trace adds one.

requirements.statement: In the live-animals set, section 5 holds the single row 'Consignment addresses', with the hint 'Consignor or Exporter, Consignee, Importer and Place of Destination' under its link; the row covers the consignment addresses page and the CPH number page, and it is the only row with a hint.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 gives the Addresses section one row, 'Consignment addresses', with that hint, and the owner's 17 November decision fixes the same words and keeps the hint as it is.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p5-031 and p5-032 show the row titled 'Consignment addresses' with the hint verbatim as the only hinted row, and repo-frontend-p5-053 shows it covering the addresses page and the CPH number page; the older traces still show 'Roles and addresses' (trace-animals-fit-p4-052, trace-e2e-p13-028), which the code has since changed. That the row also waits on every addressable animal's permanent address belongs to the identification-and-permanent-address area.

requirements.statement: The hub has a section '6. Contact address' holding the single row 'Contact address for this consignment', which reads 'Complete' once a contact address is chosen.
requirements.why: Out of scope: the design's hub has no contact address section and ends at '5. Addresses', and the live-animals hub already holds five sections with no contact address task. Whether a contact address is asked anywhere in the journey is the contact address area's decision, not the hub's.
requirements.deltaNote: The live-animals hub has no contact address section or task today (repo-frontend-p5-082, repo-frontend-p5-083); the older traces still show one (trace-animals-fit-p4-055, trace-e2e-p13-029), which c-406 sets aside.

requirements.statement: Each hub row shows one of two status tags only: a green 'Complete' when every answer the row covers is given and none of its saved answers is invalid, otherwise a blue 'To do'; there is no 'In progress', optional or other state.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 uses exactly two task states on the hub. What finishes each task is the rule of the page behind the row, decided where that page is reconciled.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p5-035 and p5-036 give exactly a green 'Complete' and a blue 'To do', with a part-answered or not-applicable row reading 'To do', and trace-animals-fit-p4-024 and trace-e2e-p13-032 show no other state today; trace-animals-fit-p4-068 records that no trace takes a row back from Complete to To do.

requirements.statement: Every row the hub shows is a link the trader can open at any time, in any order: no row is locked or shown as 'Cannot start yet', and a row that does not apply is left off the hub rather than shown locked.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 lets a trader start any task in any order.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p5-037 to p5-039 and p5-084, with trace-animals-fit-p4-025 and p4-026, show every shown row as a link, none 'Cannot start yet', nine rows openable before a commodity is chosen, and inapplicable conditional rows removed, today. This holds for the live-animals hub and the germinal copy of it; the high-risk plants Overview keeps its own gated rows, which no row of this programme changes.

requirements.statement: The hub's task list is built from the GOV.UK Task list component, one per section, with each row's status (and the consignment addresses hint) tied to its link by aria-describedby, so a screen reader moving by links hears the task, its hint and its status.
requirements.why: The prototype's custom markup does not tie status or hint to the link, which fails screen-reader users; the GOV.UK component gives the same look and meets the accessibility regulations the real service must meet.
requirements.deltaNote: trace-animals-fit-p4-023, repo-frontend-p5-017 and trace-e2e-p13-030-m1 show one GOV.UK task list per section with aria-describedby status (and hint) ids today; c-129 keeps them over the prototype's custom markup.

requirements.statement: A new notification goes from choosing the notification type to the origin page, and the first hub a trader reaches already shows 'Where is this consignment coming from?' as 'Complete'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 sends a new live-animals notification to the origin page first, not to the hub.
requirements.deltaNote: trace-animals-fit-p4-027 shows a new notification's first hub with the origin row already Complete, and trace-e2e-p13-040 shows the origin page saving on into the journey. The prototype shows an all-'To do' hub only when its URL is typed directly, which the real per-notification hub does not need to copy.

requirements.statement: A page opened from a hub row ends at the hub on 'Save and continue', so the main import reason page, the arrival details page and the consignment addresses page each return to the hub rather than going on to the next page of the journey.
requirements.why: In Design Release 2.1 a task opened from the hub comes back to the hub when saved, so the trader chooses what to do next; ruling:sam-2026-10-09 adopted this by changing only the live flow's fallback. ruling:sam-2026-11-10b held it until the save and continue work merged, and that work has merged with Save and continue going on to the next page from every start, so whether the return is still wanted is open (c-notification-hub-003).
requirements.deltaNote: Today Save and continue goes on to the next page that applies from every start, the overview included: arrival details opened from the overview goes on to the commodity search (repo-frontend-p5-046). The older traces show the run moving within a task group before returning (trace-animals-fit-p4-030, trace-e2e-p13-041). The row links already carry the service's own ?from=overview trail (repo-frontend-p5-038), so no new marker is added (c-243).

requirements.statement: A task page opened from the hub has a 'Back' link to the hub and ends with 'Save and continue', a secondary 'Save and return to overview' that saves and goes to the hub, and a 'Cancel and return to overview' link that goes to the hub without saving.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 gives every task page reached from the hub these ways back to it; DR1's rule already limits the three controls to pages the overview links to.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p5-048, with trace-e2e-p13-037 to p13-039 and p13-043, show the Back link to the hub and all three exits on task pages today, 'Cancel and return to overview' discarding what was typed and 'Save and return to overview' committing it.

requirements.statement: For a notification, the hub ends with a primary 'Review and submit' button that opens the review page, always shown and active whatever the task statuses, with nothing on the hub to say the notification is ready; submitting is still gated on the review page.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 offers the review at any time and names what is outstanding there.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p5-055 to p5-057 and trace-animals-fit-p4-059 show 'Review and submit' as the primary control, a link styled as a button (repo-frontend-p5-002), opening the review page with only the origin answered; repo-frontend-p5-058 shows no readiness banner or progress count on the hub.

requirements.statement: For a notification, the hub's secondary button is 'Return to dashboard', after 'Review and submit' in the same button group, going to the set's own notification list at the set's root in the animals frontend: /live-animals for a live-animals notification, /germinal-products for a germinal one.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's way off the hub; the prototype's 'overall dashboard' becomes the set's own list, because each notification list stays in its own frontend and is reframed in place there, and the 27 November ruling gives the germinal set its own list, copied from today's live-animals list.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p5-059 and trace-animals-fit-p4-061 show the secondary 'Return to dashboard' linking to the set base, where the set's own list is today and stays (ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p3-089, p3-103); the germinal hub's copy links to its own set root, where the germinal list's copy is (ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p3-104, ruling-sam-2026-11-27-p1-022).

requirements.statement: The hub shows only its main and secondary buttons: there is no 'Save as template' button on it.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 has no save-as-template action on the hub.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p5-055 shows the button group holding only 'Review and submit' and 'Return to dashboard' today, with nothing after them (trace-e2e-p13-034).

requirements.statement: The hub has no serious or critical WCAG 2 A/AA accessibility violations, whether it shows zero totals, a commodity with numbers owed, or non-zero totals.
requirements.why: The real service must meet the accessibility regulations; the hub already does.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p5-062 and trace-animals-fit-p4-019 show axe passing on the hub in each state today.

requirements.statement: When the hub is showing a template being created, the status strip above the heading reads 'Template' as its tag and shows the template's name beside it in place of a notification reference.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 reuses the hub to build a template and labels it as one; template mode walks the same journey pages as a notification, with no copied pages, so the template's hub is the set's own hub in template mode. The 9 October afternoon ruling never changes the shared status strip in place except for the Amend bar, so the hub switches the shared strip off in template mode and draws this header in the set's own hub template. Template mode is for the animals sets only: the plants Overview gets no template mode.
requirements.deltaNote: The hub today has no template mode: its strip shows only the notification's status tag and reference (repo-frontend-p5-061).
requirements.blockedBy: Sam must take the templates rows out of the park: ruling:sam-2026-11-04 de-prioritises templates, leaves their rows parked in themes/type-question-and-templates and names no condition or date for picking them up again.

requirements.statement: When the hub is showing a template being created, the task list is headed 'Template task list'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 heads a template's task list after the template rather than the notification, and the owner's 19 November decision spells 'task list' as two words, the GOV.UK spelling, wherever the heading appears.
requirements.blockedBy: Sam must take the templates rows out of the park: ruling:sam-2026-11-04 de-prioritises templates, leaves their rows parked in themes/type-question-and-templates and names no condition or date for picking them up again.

requirements.statement: When the hub is showing a template being created, the Documents section is left out and the addresses section after it is numbered '4. Addresses'.
requirements.why: A template holds no shipment-specific documents in Design Release 2.1, whose hub ends at the addresses section, and the owner's 17 November decision fixes the addresses section's words while keeping its number in the sequence.
requirements.blockedBy: Sam must take the templates rows out of the park: ruling:sam-2026-11-04 de-prioritises templates, leaves their rows parked in themes/type-question-and-templates and names no condition or date for picking them up again.

The real service's own markers stand, because they are its architecture rather than the prototype's: the row links carry ?from=overview (repo-frontend-p5-038, repo-plantsfrontend-p2-031) and 'Save and return to overview' posts exit=hub, which ruling-sam-2026-10-09-p1-089 keeps. Which page each row opens still follows the prototype's row claims (prototype-dr2-1-source-p12-021 to p12-032, p12-121); only the marker claims are overruled, trace-prototype-dr2-1-p12-020 among them because its row-to-page list is carried by those source claims. trace-e2e-p13-041-m1 shows the real flow returning without a marker on re-entry and is kept.

Plants already makes the same checks on both buttons, so nothing is built; the plants decision ledger entry d-059 carries the evidence, and repo-plantsfrontend-p2-138 shows the save landing on the Overview. ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p3-063 is not overruled either, because its other clauses (arrival details' own rules are animals only, and plants takes the return to the overview) still stand; only its lenient-save clause falls with p3-027.

conflicts.outcome: The owner's 19 November decision ranks above the prototype and fixes the heading as 'Notification task list' in the live animals and plants services alike; the live-animals hub already renders it that way (repo-frontend-p5-015) and the plants Overview too (repo-plantsfrontend-p2-003). The ground the ruling gives, the GOV.UK spelling of 'task list', applies wherever the heading names a task list, so a template's heading reads 'Template task list' (req-815). Only the spelling is set aside: prototype-dr2-1-source-p12-017, trace-prototype-dr2-1-p12-009 and prototype-dr2-1-specs-p6-057 still back the hub having a task list heading of its own and its five section headings, and p12-017 still backs a template naming its own, so none is overruled.

conflicts.outcome: The repository ranks above both trace sets, and the code is the later record: the animals frontend has since landed the 'Notification task list' heading, the '5. Addresses' section, the 'Consignment addresses' row and the 'Main import reason' row title (repo-frontend-p5-015, p5-024, p5-031, p5-082), and has removed the contact address section and task (repo-frontend-p5-082, p5-083), as the design also has no contact address section (prototype-dr2-1-source-p12-122). The traces, recorded at an earlier commit, no longer say what the hub shows on those points. Each requirement takes its delta from the repository claims. The claims whose whole content is superseded are set aside: the one-word heading and the contact address section. The others are left standing because they are still right about everything else they say: trace-animals-fit-p4-052 and trace-e2e-p13-028 still give the row's hint, trace-animals-fit-p4-028 and trace-e2e-p13-020 still give section 1's first two rows, trace-animals-fit-p4-021 and trace-e2e-p13-018 still give the first four section headings and their order, and trace-animals-fit-p4-026 still shows every row openable before a commodity is chosen. The out-of-scope contact address requirement (req-803) keeps the set-aside contact claims to record what was dropped.

conflicts.about: What the status strip's type label reads on the high-risk plants pages: the prototype's plants labels ('Plants for planting', 'Potatoes (seed and ware)', 'Wood products'), or plants' own commodity type wording.

positions.says: The strip prefixes the reference with the notification type's label, 'Live animals', 'Germinal products', 'Plants for planting', 'Potatoes (seed and ware)' or 'Wood products', and shows the reference alone for any other type.
The strip reads 'Live animals - <reference>' beside the Draft tag.

conflicts.outcome: The 9 October afternoon ruling ranks above the prototype: plants takes the type label in the same increment as the animals sets, but in its own words, so the strip reads the label plants' own commodity type question gives the chosen type (its 'Wood and cut trees', not the prototype's 'Wood products'), and shows the reference alone until a commodity type is chosen, as the prototype does for a type it has no label for. The live-animals and germinal-products sets read 'Live animals' and 'Germinal products' as the prototype gives them (req-notification-hub-001). Nothing is overruled: prototype-dr2-1-source-p12-114 still backs the animals labels and the label-then-reference pattern.

Where the gross weight is asked is the commodity-details area's to build.

conflicts.about: Whether 'Save and continue' on a page opened from the overview returns to the overview, now that the save and continue work the 10 November ruling waited on has merged with Save and continue going on to the next page that applies from every start.

positions.says: The return links row stays blocked until the save and continue work has merged.
A page opened from its overview task returns to the overview on Save and continue.
Arrival details opened from the hub returns to the hub on Save and continue rather than going on to transit countries.
Arrival details opened from the overview goes on, on Save and continue, to the 'What are you importing?' commodity search.

conflicts.outcome: Precedence does not settle it. The 9 October ruling and the design return an overview-opened page to the overview, but the 10 November ruling, which ranks above both, held that change until the save and continue work merged without saying what follows. That work (EUDPA-774) has merged in the live animals and plants frontends with the opposite rule, written into both frontends' routing docs and the plants decisions ledger: Save and continue goes on to the next page that applies from every start, the overview included (repo-frontend-p5-046). Building the return to the overview would reverse a rule the target repos now record, so the owner is asked, with the repos' rule kept by default.
conflicts.question: Now that the save and continue work has merged with Save and continue going on through the journey from every start, should a page opened from the overview still return to the overview on Save and continue, in live animals, the germinal copy and plants?
conflicts.default: No: Save and continue goes on to the next page that applies from every start, as the merged work built, in live animals, in the germinal products copy and in plants; 'Save and return to overview' and 'Cancel and return to overview' stay the ways back to the overview, and the return-to-overview change (req-808, req-1934) is not built.
